result.title: Genesis Steering: Better Activation Steering Through Training Data
result.summary: Activation steering controls large language models at inference time, but its effectiveness depends on the choice of reference data. We introduce genesis steering, which derives a genesis vector from contrastive examples in the model's own fine-tuning data. When these data are unavailable, we draw on the membership inference literature to identify likely training examples and construct a proxy dataset. We establish two theoretical results on optimal displacement to the decision boundary and reduced proxy-estimation bias. We evaluate genesis steering and membership-based proxy construction on Tülu-3-8B, whose fine-tuning data are publicly available, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as a control. We find that safety data from Tülu-3-8B's training mixture yield stronger steering than external datasets on both models. On Tülu-3-8B, membership scores largely agree in identifying training examples, and vectors built from top-ranked examples achieve competitive performance against random subsets of the same size. In contrast, the results on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct hint that a MIA method will only have a positive effect if the mean direction shift with MIA-filtered in-distribution data is much less severe than the direction shift with OoD data.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 genesis steering：从模型自身微调数据中的对比样例导出「genesis 向量」用于推理期激活引导，数据不可得时借助成员推断（MIA）筛选疑似训练样本构造代理数据，并给出关于最优决策边界位移与代理估计偏差的两条理论结果，在 Tülu-3-8B 与 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用对比样例与分布内数据构造方向向量来干预内部激活」的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的引导、对比式监督数据选择与视觉证据筛选提供可核查线索，但论文为纯文本且针对安全引导，与多模态推理状态的关联尚待验证。
